documents.title: The hidden cost of free returns
documents.text:
For more than a decade, online retailers have competed by promising free returns, and shoppers have responded by ordering several sizes of the same garment and sending most of them back. Industry estimates suggest that nearly a third of clothing bought online is returned, a rate roughly three times that of purchases made in stores. Yet this convenience is proving increasingly expensive, and a number of well-known companies have begun to charge for it.

The costs are not limited to postage. Each returned item must be inspected, cleaned, repackaged and restocked, a process that can cost a retailer between ten and twenty dollars. Items that cannot be resold, including those returned after being worn, are often discarded. A study by the Verhoeven Institute estimated that the carbon emissions generated by returns in the clothing sector now exceed those of a mid-sized airline.

Retailers are experimenting with alternatives. Some now show customers how a garment fits models of different builds, while others offer a small discount to shoppers who choose to keep items. Consumer advocate Lena Strand cautions, however, that fees may deter people on low incomes more than anyone else. "If returning costs money, the people who can least afford a mistake will be the ones most reluctant to take a risk," she says. Many analysts expect a compromise in which returns remain free at physical stores but carry a modest fee online.

questions.prompt: What is the main point of the article?
choices: Online shoppers are buying fewer clothes than before
Free returns are becoming too costly for sellers to maintain
Stores have started to accept returns from other firms
Carbon emissions from airlines are falling quickly
questions.explanation: The article explains why retailers are starting to charge for returns, given high processing and environmental costs.

questions.prompt: What does the article say about returned items?
choices: They are cleaned by the customers before posting
They are always resold at a lower price
They are sent to charities in most cases
Some of them are thrown away rather than sold again
questions.explanation: Items that cannot be resold, including those worn, are often discarded.

questions.prompt: What is Ms. Strand's concern?
choices: Fees for returns could unfairly hit poorer buyers
Retailers will refuse to refund customers who ask
Customers will stop buying anything on the Internet
Information about fit is not accurate for all sizes
questions.explanation: She says that people who can least afford a mistake will be reluctant to take a risk if returns cost money.

questions.prompt: The word "deter" in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to
choices: inform
compensate
discourage
satisfy
questions.explanation: Fees may make low-income shoppers less willing to order, so they 'discourage' them.

documents.title: Reminder: Quarterly inventory count
documents.text:
To: Warehouse and store supervisors
From: Ivana Petrov, Inventory Control
Subject: Quarterly count on Saturday 14 June

Dear colleagues,

This is a reminder that the quarterly inventory count will take place on Saturday 14 June. All stores will close at 3 p.m. on Friday 13 June, and the warehouse will not dispatch any orders after noon on that day. Counting will begin at 7 a.m. on Saturday and should be completed by 4 p.m.

Please remember the following points. Teams of two will count each aisle, one person counting and the other recording, and the teams will be rotated after lunch so that every section is counted by two different pairs. Any difference of more than two percent between the system and the physical count must be recounted before a team leaves the aisle. Damaged goods should be placed in the yellow cages and not counted, as they will be assessed separately by quality control.

Overtime for the day will be paid at one and a half times the normal rate, and a meal will be provided at noon. Supervisors who have not yet submitted their staffing plans should send them to me by Wednesday so that I can confirm the assignments. Please note that annual leave is not available for the count day except in an emergency.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the e-mail?
choices: To announce the opening of another large warehouse
To report a loss of goods noticed in the system
To prepare supervisors for a stock count
To change the pay rates that apply to overtime
questions.explanation: It reminds supervisors of arrangements for the quarterly count.

questions.prompt: Why are the teams rotated after lunch?
choices: So each aisle is checked by two pairs
To give each worker a different task to perform
To prevent people from working too long in one place
To make it easy to count the damaged goods apart
questions.explanation: Every section is counted by two different pairs.

questions.prompt: What should happen to goods that are damaged?
choices: They should be counted twice
They should be sent back to suppliers
They should be sold at a discount
They should be put aside and not included
questions.explanation: They go into the yellow cages and are not counted.

questions.prompt: What is NOT stated about Saturday's work?
choices: Workers will be given a meal at midday
Employees will receive a day off in exchange
Extra hours will be paid at a higher rate
Staff leave is generally not allowed
questions.explanation: Overtime is paid at one and a half times the rate; no day off is mentioned.

documents.title: Messages between Dana Whitfield and a contractor
documents.text:
Dana Whitfield (11:05 a.m.): Hi Luis, it's Dana from Birchwood Café. The plumber came this morning and says the leak in the kitchen is coming from the pipe under the floor, not the sink. He estimates it will take two days to repair, and we'd need to close.
Luis Moreno (11:08 a.m.): Understood. If the floor has to be opened, I'd suggest we also replace the damaged tiles near the freezer while it's up. It will save you paying for a second visit.
Dana Whitfield (11:10 a.m.): Good idea. How long would the tiles add?
Luis Moreno (11:12 a.m.): About a day, plus the time for the adhesive to dry. I could do it on Tuesday and Wednesday if you close on Monday for the plumber, and you'd reopen on Thursday morning.
Dana Whitfield (11:15 a.m.): That means four days without income, which is hard. Could we keep the front counter open for coffee and pastries?
Luis Moreno (11:17 a.m.): The work area is behind the kitchen door, so yes, if the plumber isolates the water supply to the dining area only. I'd need to check with him.
Dana Whitfield (11:18 a.m.): Please do. I'll send you the measurements for the tiles tonight.

questions.prompt: What problem has Ms. Whitfield discovered?
choices: The freezer next to the sink has stopped working
The leak starts below the kitchen floor
The sink has to be replaced completely this week
The plumber has canceled his planned visit today
questions.explanation: The plumber says the leak is from the pipe under the floor, not the sink.

questions.prompt: Why does Mr. Moreno propose replacing the tiles?
choices: The old tiles cause a danger to staff
The adhesive needs to be renewed each year
The freezer is being moved to another place
The floor will already be open for the repair
questions.explanation: He says that it will save a second visit while the floor is up.

questions.prompt: What does Ms. Whitfield mean when she writes, "which is hard" at 11:15 a.m.?
choices: The closure would cause money problems for her
The tiles are too heavy for her to carry alone
The work is too technical for her to understand
The plumber is unavailable until the following week
questions.explanation: She says four days without income is hard, referring to the closure's effect on money.

questions.prompt: What does Mr. Moreno need to do next?
choices: Order the new tiles from a supplier in town
Tell the plumber to begin his work on Monday
See if part of the café could stay open
Send Ms. Whitfield a complete list of measurements
questions.explanation: He agrees to check with the plumber whether the water supply can be isolated so the counter can remain open.

documents.title: Orchard Hill Retirement Village
documents.text:
Discover a new chapter at Orchard Hill, a friendly community of 140 apartments and cottages set in landscaped grounds twelve minutes from the town center. Our residents enjoy a clubhouse with a library and café, a heated indoor pool and a weekly program of activities that ranges from gardening to guest lectures. A nurse is on site every day, and emergency call systems are installed in every home.

One-bedroom apartments are available from 1,450 dollars a month, including all utilities, a weekly cleaning service and use of our shuttle to the town. Two-bedroom cottages start at 2,100 dollars. We welcome pets under 10 kg. There is no entry fee, and residents can leave at any time with one month's notice. Meals in the dining room are optional and cost 9 dollars each. Book a visit before 30 April and enjoy lunch with our residents, and a free night's stay in our guest suite for family visiting from out of town.

questions.prompt: What is the advertisement mainly about?
choices: A medical clinic that specializes in complex surgery
A hotel with a heated swimming pool and a café
A housing community designed for older residents
A group of apartments rented mainly to students
questions.explanation: It promotes apartments, services and activities for retirees.

questions.prompt: What is included in the monthly price of an apartment?
choices: Utility bills and a weekly cleaning service
Three meals prepared every day in the dining room
Medical treatment given by a nurse each day
A stay in the guest suite for family visitors
questions.explanation: The one-bedroom price includes all utilities and a weekly cleaning service.

questions.prompt: What can be inferred about the dining room?
choices: It is closed on the weekend and on holidays
It is covered by the monthly rent in all cases
It is open only to visitors who come on a tour
People living there can decide whether to eat in
questions.explanation: Meals are optional at 9 dollars each.

questions.prompt: What is offered to people who visit before the end of April?
choices: A free month in one of the two-bedroom cottages
A lunch with residents and a night for relatives
A discount applied to the first year's rent
A guided tour of the town center by shuttle
questions.explanation: They enjoy lunch with residents and a free night's stay in the guest suite for visiting family.

documents.title: Request for supplier quotation: office furniture
documents.text:
To: Hartwell Office Solutions
From: Beatriz Carvalho, Facilities Manager, Meridian Legal
Subject: Quotation for new office furniture

Dear Hartwell team,

Meridian Legal is moving to new premises on 1 September, and we require furniture for forty workstations, a reception area and two meeting rooms. We would like adjustable-height desks, ergonomic chairs with at least a five-year warranty, and a reception desk with a built-in storage area. Delivery and assembly must be completed by 28 August, since our staff will need time to move in.

We would appreciate a detailed quotation, including delivery and assembly, by 20 June. Our budget for the project is 45,000 dollars, and we will give preference to suppliers who can demonstrate that their products are made from certified or recycled materials.

Best regards,
Beatriz Carvalho

documents.title: Quotation for Meridian Legal
documents.text:
Dear Ms. Carvalho,

Thank you for your inquiry. I am pleased to enclose our quotation. Forty adjustable-height desks cost 560 dollars each, and forty Ergo-Pro chairs 340 dollars each; the chairs carry a seven-year warranty. The reception desk is 3,900 dollars and the two meeting-room tables, 1,600 dollars each. Delivery and assembly are charged at 2,200 dollars in total, and all items are made from FSC-certified timber and recycled steel.

Our lead time is eight weeks from the date of order, which means that we would need your confirmation by 25 June to meet the 28 August deadline. If your budget is tight, the Ergo-Lite chair at 270 dollars is a suitable alternative, though its warranty is limited to three years.

Sincerely,
Ravi Menon, Hartwell Office Solutions

documents.title: Re: Quotation for Meridian Legal
documents.text:
Dear Mr. Menon,

Thank you for the quotation. The total exceeds our budget by a small amount, and we cannot accept the shorter warranty. Could you offer a discount of ten percent on the desks if we increase the order to forty-five? We would then have spares for the growth we expect. Please also confirm that the reception desk can be delivered on 21 August, as our contractor will have finished by then.

Regards,
Beatriz Carvalho

questions.prompt: What does Ms. Carvalho require from the supplier?
choices: Furniture made to a fully customized design
Goods put in place before the staff move in
A free sample of each type of chair on offer
A promise to remove the furniture of the old office
questions.explanation: Delivery and assembly must be completed by 28 August, before the move on 1 September.

questions.prompt: What is the total of the quotation for the items requested?
choices: 42,100 dollars
43,900 dollars
47,500 dollars
45,300 dollars
questions.explanation: Desks 40 x 560 = 22,400; chairs 40 x 340 = 13,600; reception 3,900; tables 2 x 1,600 = 3,200; delivery 2,200. Total 45,300, slightly above the 45,000 budget.

questions.prompt: What is the problem with the Ergo-Lite chair, according to Ms. Carvalho?
choices: Its warranty is shorter than she wants
It costs more than the Ergo-Pro
It is not made from recycled materials
It cannot be delivered by August
questions.explanation: She says she cannot accept the shorter warranty.

questions.prompt: What can be inferred about Hartwell's products?
choices: They are cheaper than those sold by rival firms
They are manufactured in less than a week
They fit the buyer's environmental wishes
They are available only during the spring season
questions.explanation: Mr. Menon says all items are made from certified timber and recycled steel, which matches her stated preference.

questions.prompt: By when must Ms. Carvalho decide to have the furniture on time?
choices: 20 June
21 August
25 June
28 August
questions.explanation: The lead time is eight weeks, so confirmation is needed by 25 June.
